title: Extension closure of quasi-coherent cohomology on a localized open site
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an open, and $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ a short exact sequence of integer-indexed complexes of module sheaves on the localized open site over $U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If every $H^j(A)$ and $H^j(C)$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], then every $H^n(B)$ is quasi-coherent. None of the complexes need be bounded.

source.place: Tags 0117 (long exact cohomology sequence) and 01IE (extension closure); kernel and cokernel closure on the open subscheme.

proof.text: Transport the exact five-term cohomology sequence to U.toScheme through Scheme.Modules.overEquiv. The equivalence and its inverse preserve quasi-coherence: both are pushforwards along continuous equivalences of localized open sites and carry the unit module to the unit module.

Define the quasi-coherent object property on U.toScheme.Modules. Kernel, cokernel and extension closure give its weak Serre-class instances. Use the proved ObjectProperty.prop_of_exact_of_exact_of_exact on the transported five terms H^(n-1)(C), H^n(A), H^n(B), H^n(C), H^(n+1)(A). This is the cokernel-as-subobject and kernel-as-quotient argument. Transport the result back by the inverse equivalence and its unit isomorphism.
